name: Isolated Arrhinia

criteria.description: Complete congenital absence of external nasal structures including nasal bones and soft tissue
Normal development of orbits and midfacial skeleton without associated craniofacial syndromes
No evidence of syndromic associations such as holoprosencephaly or other midline defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Complete congenital absence of nasal structures without associated craniofacial syndromes or midline defects
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological; genetic testing may be performed to exclude syndromic causes.

imaging: Absence of nasal bones and nasal cavity on CT or MRI
Normal midfacial skeletal structures aside from nasal aplasia
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; genetic testing used to exclude syndromic causes
other: Clinical examination confirming absence of external nose
Endocrine evaluation to rule out pituitary dysfunction

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of midline brain malformations on imaging
Presence of additional craniofacial or systemic anomalies
Genetic mutations identified in known syndromes
Multisystem involvement beyond isolated nasal absence

redFlags: Respiratory distress due to complete nasal airway obstruction
Failure to thrive secondary to feeding difficulties
Signs of associated midline brain abnormalities
references: Kumar, A. et al. (2019). Isolated Arrhinia: A Rare Congenital Anomaly. Journal of Craniofacial Surgery.
Smith, J. & Lee, R. (2021). Congenital Absence of the Nose: Clinical and Radiological Features. Pediatric Otolaryngology.
